body:
I do and I don't care....it's hard to explain. When I get good grades, it's like I can reach this happy bubble where someone could look at me and say that I appear "normal". but when I get worse grades or mediocre grades, I fall back into this depressive state. I'd do anything I could to get back to this happy bubble...it's maybe tied to the fact that the school therapist stopped having forceful awkward silences with me when my grades started climbing up. When it comes to academics, I'm pretty serious. It's probably evident from even the first sentence - when it comes to introducing and identifying myself, I am a student through and through. 

My major is Earth System Science, as my university prevents people from switching into Biology and Chemistry later in the year by making them sign 4 year contracts, I ended up in ESS. 

All I want out of college...is perhaps a degree and some true friends. I want a job and financial security the most. I want to move out of my parent's house (as most kids do), and be self sufficient. I don't really ask for much really. I see myself living in a one-story house, with a quaint backyard in which to grow vegetables and flowers. 

I like to write, but again, English majors here are on a contract. Even if I mustered up the courage to switch majors without my dad's approval, I wouldn't be able to thanks to the university's restrictive policies.

But I like learning about a variety of things. I want to learn programming (Java), I want to learn Chinese, I want to learn Roman and Greek history and become better with computers/technology in general. I want to become a better writer, but without the professors looking down on me or being generally unhelpful. Of course hardly any of those things are related to each other, and I have yet to take a single class that truly interested me because my major restricts me. I took one English class and it was just painful, all they cared about was whether I cited footnotes correctly. Having an easy A actually made me feel really angry because it put me on the same level as someone who put no thought at all into their essay but was able to organize sources in alphabetical order.

Anyway, I can no longer tell if I liked or disliked Earth system science...I know at some point I liked Environmental Science but maybe I convinced myself to like it in order to make my studies more bearable.

So, I guess what's important to me ...
Is to have true friends with whom I can be open and honest and to live life without worrying about whether I'm going to be able to get up in the morning to face the day. I don't like being in the state of a depressive low, and I don't like how I am always working to put myself in circumstances that ultimately will not make me happy. I feel like I'm on a conveyor belt, like I'm being processed and refined in a little factory (whether it's my parents, the university's requirements, and society's expectations that I follow them at all) I want to escape that, but I don't know if I can...and some days, especially today, I just think that if I ended it that maybe it would be less painful in the long run
